note: Weekly pool for the Useful Life For your reading card. types: life_area. wants: reading_goal or pace. paces: hard filter.

items.title: Your next read: Tiny Habits by BJ Fogg
items.text: Built for people who want to use what they read. Each chapter ends with a small exercise, so read 1 a week and do it before moving on.

items.title: Your next read: The Power of Habit by Charles Duhigg
items.text: The book that made the habit loop famous: cue, routine, reward. Story-driven and fast to read, so it suits a quick pace.

items.title: Your next read: Deep Work by Cal Newport
items.text: Part 2 is the useful half: 4 rules for protecting focused hours. Read part 1 quickly, then slow down for the rules.

items.title: Your next read: Four Thousand Weeks by Oliver Burkeman
items.text: A calm book about time instead of another productivity system. Short chapters that each stand alone, so it works even at 1 chapter a week.

items.title: Your next read: The Psychology of Money by Morgan Housel
items.text: Short chapters, 1 idea each, no spreadsheets. Easy to finish at any pace, and the compounding chapter is the one to reread.

items.title: Your next read: I Will Teach You to Be Rich by Ramit Sethi
items.text: A step-by-step money setup: accounts, automatic savings, spending on what you love. Read it with your banking app open.

items.title: Your next read: The Simple Path to Wealth by JL Collins
items.text: Started as letters to his daughter about investing. Plain, opinionated and quick for a fast reader.

items.title: Your next read: Man's Search for Meaning by Viktor Frankl
items.text: Short enough to finish in a few sittings, and one of the most reread nonfiction books there is. Start here if you read slowly.

items.title: Your next read: The Obstacle Is the Way by Ryan Holiday
items.text: Stoic ideas through short stories of people who turned problems into progress. Each chapter is a few pages, perfect for a daily read.

items.title: Your next read: Mindset by Carol Dweck
items.text: The fixed vs growth mindset book. The first 3 chapters carry the idea, and the rest shows it in work, sport and parenting.
